# Kyoto Budget Trip Overview

A 5-day Kyoto plan for 2 adults from **Seoul to Kyoto, 2026-04-10 to 2026-04-14**, built to stay within **USD 2,400 total** excluding shopping.
It prioritizes **temples, local food, one low-walking day, early evenings, and under 12,000 steps/day**.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary

| Day | Focus | Transit | Estimated Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Day 1 | Arrival + Higashiyama soft start | Flight to Osaka/KIX or Itami, then airport train/bus to Kyoto | **$420** |
| Day 2 | Arashiyama temples and river area | JR train + local bus / short taxi hops | **$360** |
| Day 3 | Fushimi Inari + central Kyoto food streets | JR/Nara Line + subway | **$310** |
| Day 4 | Relaxed day: museums, markets, easy shrine visits | Subway + taxi as needed | **$280** |
| Day 5 | Northern Kyoto temples + departure | Subway/bus to station, airport transfer | **$330** |

## 5-Day Kyoto Plan

### Day 1: Arrival, Gion, and an Easy Temple Evening
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/airplane.svg
- **Morning:** Fly Seoul to Kansai International Airport; take the JR Haruka or airport bus to Kyoto Station.
- **Afternoon:** Check in, rest, then do a gentle walk through **Gion** and **Yasaka Shrine**.
- **Evening:** Early dinner near Pontocho or Gion; keep it light and close to the hotel.
- **Food:** Kyoto-style obanzai set meal or tofu hot pot.
- **Rainy-day backup:** Kyoto Station area shopping/dining, Kyoto Tower, and a café break instead of Gion walking.
- **Estimated cost:** Flight/transfer $260, lodging $110, food $50 = **$420**

### Day 2: Arashiyama Temples, Bamboo, and Riverside Views
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Morning:** Go early to **Tenryu-ji** and the **Arashiyama Bamboo Grove** before crowds build.
- **Afternoon:** Visit **Okochi Sanso Garden** or take a slow river-area break; use a short taxi if needed to reduce walking.
- **Evening:** Return to central Kyoto for a simple dinner near Kyoto Station.
- **Food:** Yuba (tofu skin) lunch and matcha dessert.
- **Rainy-day backup:** Tenryu-ji, Arashiyama Monkey Park skip option, and indoor tea/café time near Arashiyama Station.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/6/60/A_Japanese_Macaque_at_Arashiyama_Monkey_Park_Iwatayama%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Rainy-day backup:** Tenryu-ji, Arashiyama Monkey Park skip option, and indoor tea/café time near Arashiyama Station, Kyoto, Japan
- **Estimated cost:** Transit $20, entries $40, food $60, lodging $110, buffer $130 = **$360**

### Day 3: Fushimi Inari, Sake District, and Local Eats
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/signpost-split.svg
- **Morning:** Visit **Fushimi Inari Taisha** early; do only the lower and mid sections to stay under the walking target.
- **Afternoon:** Head to **Fushimi sake district** for a tasting lunch or a relaxed canal-side stroll.
- **Evening:** Dinner around Kyoto Station or Nishiki Market area, then an early return.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Evening:** Dinner around Kyoto Station or Nishiki Market area, then an early return, Kyoto, Japan
- **Food:** Inari sushi, yudofu, and sake-friendly small plates.
- **Rainy-day backup:** Skip the hillside climb and focus on the shrine entrance, museum-style sake tasting, and indoor food stops.
- **Estimated cost:** Transit $15, entries/tastings $45, food $70, lodging $110, buffer $70 = **$310**

### Day 4: Relaxed Low-Walking Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/house.svg
- **Morning:** Start late with a hotel breakfast, then visit **Nishiki Market** for a slow food-focused morning.
- **Afternoon:** Choose one easy indoor or low-walk stop: **Kyoto International Manga Museum**, **Kyoto Railway Museum**, or a long café break.
- **Evening:** Early kaiseki-lite dinner or set meal near your hotel; finish before dark.
- **Food:** Market snacks, grilled fish set, seasonal sweets.
- **Rainy-day backup:** This day already works as the main backup day; keep everything indoors and taxi-friendly.
- **Estimated cost:** Transit $15, entries $30, food $65, lodging $110, buffer $60 = **$280**

### Day 5: Northern Kyoto Temples, Then Departure
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Morning:** Visit **Kinkaku-ji** early for the best light and fewer crowds.
- **Afternoon:** If energy allows, add **Ryoan-ji**; otherwise enjoy a slow lunch and head back to collect bags.
- **Evening:** Transfer to the airport and return to Seoul.
- **Food:** Simple noodle lunch or temple-area set meal.
- **Rainy-day backup:** If weather is poor, replace Kinkaku-ji/Ryoan-ji with Kyoto Station shopping, tea, and a final indoor meal.
- **Estimated cost:** Transit $35, entries $20, food $55, airport transfer $120, buffer $100 = **$330**

## Budget Fit and Practical Notes

- **Estimated total:** **$1,700–$2,000**
- **Budget ceiling:** **$2,400**
- **Comfort buffer remaining:** about **$400–$700**
- This leaves room for:
  - one nicer dinner,
  - a taxi on one tired day,
  - extra snacks or admission fees,
  - seasonal price changes in April.

### Transit Suggestions
- Use **JR + subway + occasional taxi** rather than rental car.
- For airport access, compare:
  - **KIX → Kyoto:** Haruka or airport bus
  - **Itami → Kyoto:** airport bus or taxi depending on flight timing
- Keep a **single hotel base near Kyoto Station, Gion, or Kawaramachi** to reduce transfers and walking.

### Walking Control
- Front-load the most walk-heavy sights early in the day.
- Use taxis for short hops in Arashiyama, Fushimi, or between clustered temple areas.
- Plan one sit-down café break daily to keep steps manageable.
